about.what: Everything about THIS installation that is not geometry: which arm answers on which address and DDS domain, which arms are bolted in, where the drawing server is, and how hard the pen presses. Geometry (poses, parks, pens) is in config/rig.json and is never repeated here.
about.addresses_source: control-box IPs and domains from the 2026-09-09 control-stack briefing (section 5, arm_registry.py). Arm 71 had no IP on 2026-09-15 (HARDWARE_DAY1 section 1.6). Verify every row with `aris-robot identify` before the first run.
about.mounted_source: HARDWARE_DAY1 (2026-09-16): arms 31 and 71 were mounted. Set `mounted` true for an arm only when it hangs in its place in rig.json and answers on its address.
about.inverted_note: rig.json hangs all six arms upside down; `inverted` true makes the launch hang the robot model from the frame (mount_to_world, as the operator patches do).

ros.joint_prefix_note: joint names are <joint_prefix>_joint1..7; the briefing notes one stack that used fr3v2

force.source: graphite mine (2 mm, 4H / H): band 0.7-1.0 N in 9 levels, force cap 3.5 N on arm 13 (control-stack briefing 2026-09-09, sections 9 and 10). A gel pen uses 0.6-1.0 N and a cap of 2.0-2.6 N.
force.ramp_note: the force grows from zero to the setpoint over the first 2 mm of a drawing motion (Diemut's slide-in)
force.tare_note: the force estimate in the air is not zero (2.5 N on arm 17 in the old stack was the clamp); a larger reading than this refuses the landing
force.servo_ki_note: 1/s: the force servo trims the fed-forward force toward the setpoint from the force estimate with a 1 s time constant (orchestrator, 2026-09-30). 0 turns it off: the force is then fed forward without correction.
force.sign_note: +1: the paper pushing the pen up reads positive. The old stack needed -1 on arm 13; check with `aris-robot touch` before trusting a reading.
